answer: What breaks first is the assumption that a sponsor can vouch for its own recruit. Give each new identity a deposit equal to the compute its first three tasks will burn, keep the handler who introduced it off its audit panel, and require two disagreeing peers before the deposit releases. Every signature lands in the opal record. A farm pays the deposit, waits for strangers, and cannot reuse the same reviewers. At the next summit the arithmetic is plain: one clone costs a bond plus two unrelated opinions, and the tide of free registrations stops.
